title: Evaluation of new OAE- and ASSR-measurement methods for newborn hearing screening
summary: The study “Evaluation of new OAE and ASSR measurement methods for newborn hearing screening” investigates new methods for early hearing diagnosis in newborns. The aim is to evaluate certain parameters, such as the validity, measurement duration, and practicability of innovative measurement methods in comparison to established methods. The study is being conducted in several phases with voluntary participation after informed consent has been obtained from the parents. The measurements are performed by qualified specialists and applied in random order to avoid bias. The results should provide information about the applicability of the new methods in everyday clinical practice.
conditions: Hearing loss due to conductive or sensorineural hearing impairment, other hearing loss, congenital or early childhood hearing loss

interventions.name: The study population consists of infants aged 0 to 6 months who are presented at the clinic for newborn hearing screening, follow-up examination of an abnormal newborn hearing screening result, or follow-up examination of an abnormal (external) follow-up examination result after an abnormal newborn

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Infants who are presented to the clinic for newborn hearing screening, follow-up testing of an abnormal newborn hearing screening result, or follow-up testing of an abnormal (external) follow-up examination after a previously abnormal newborn hearing screening result.
Parental consent: Parents must give their informed consent before the study can begin.
Exclusion criteria:
• Children with serious health problems that would not allow for an extension of the examination, e.g., severe heart defects, severe neurological diseases
• Routine diagnostics that cannot be performed in full
• Children whose parents/medical representatives do not give informed consent
